content: Letter 29, to Sayyid Aḥmad, i.e., Amīr Sayyid Aḥmad Kārkiyā (ca. 831-32/1428-29, Gilan): Ibn Turka praises the amir's patronage of scholars and Sufis and congratulates him on a conquest (TMN/MS pp. 23-24, TMN/D pp. 194-96). MK's footnote: the Kārkiyā were Zaydī sayyids ruling Gilan; under Shāhrukh Sayyid Riżā Kārkiyā (d. 829/1426) ruled first, then Sayyid Nāṣir at Lahijan and Sayyid Aḥmad at Ranikuh; Sayyid Aḥmad is the most likely addressee, since the language shows an autonomous ruler and the letter belongs to the northern exile.
